## Summary of the last run

The page is largely correct. The main genuine problem is in the remark on computation: the assertion that over a field $\mathrm{SL}_{n}$ is generated by type (III) elementary matrices alone is false (already for $n=2$), and should be corrected to generation by all elementary matrices (with the $SK_{1}$ remark retained for rings). Other supplements and remarks (Schubert cells, Cholesky/QR, fill-in, orbit/Grassmann description) were checked and are acceptable.

## Issues

### ISSUE-0001 [Open] SL_n generated by type (III) elementary matrices over a field
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** remark 計算量と可換環上の消去
- **Detail:** The remark claims that over a field $\mathrm{SL}_{n}$ is generated by type (III) elementary matrices alone. This is false for $n=2$: the elementary matrices $T_{12}(c)$ and $T_{21}(c)$ are upper/lower unit triangular, and products of these (in $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$) are exactly the matrices $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ with $a\neq 0$ (or the analogous condition), so matrices such as $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ are not products of type (III) matrices. The correct statement is that $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(k)$ is generated by elementary matrices (including type (II) $D_{i}(c)$ with $c^{n}=1$ adjustments), or that $E_{n}(k)=\mathrm{SL}_{n}(k)$ for a field and $n\ge 2$ where $E_{n}$ is generated by elementary transvections together with diagonal matrices; the claim as stated (only type (III)) fails.
- **Proposed fix:** Over a field, $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(k)$ is generated by elementary matrices (transvections $T_{ij}(c)$ together with suitable diagonal elementary matrices); it is not generated by type (III) matrices alone (e.g. $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ is not a product of type (III) matrices). Over a general commutative ring the failure of $E_{n}(R)=\mathrm{SL}_{n}(R)$ is measured by $SK_{1}$.
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (8ccef3d)
